checks.goal: Establish whether this run's evidence can be trusted: the agent is reachable and every collector is running.
checks.procedure: Read health.context.collectors and the agent.* checks first. A collector that is not running makes every observed kind it feeds unknown, not healthy; a heartbeat that is not healthy makes every agent-backed section unknown.
checks.criterion: heartbeat is healthy and every collector reports running.

checks.goal: Detect stale observations before reasoning on them.
checks.procedure: Compare every kind in health.context.freshness with the run's time window and with the observation timestamps carried by each read. There is no universal freshness limit: judge per source.
checks.criterion: each kind's newest_observed_at lies inside the run's time window; a stale kind is reported as unknown, never as healthy.

checks.goal: Find where the effective configuration has drifted from the desired state.
checks.procedure: Run the drift checks (drift.nfs-conf needs the standard profile: quick skips it), then drift.report for the full desired-vs-observed picture and config_history.diff for what changed since the last snapshot.
checks.criterion: no drift between desired and effective exports, netplan and nfs.conf; a drift row names the file and the differing keys.

checks.goal: Compare the host against the selected baseline profile's expectations.
checks.procedure: Obtain the baseline engine report for the selected profile and read every section, not only the overall status. Resolve each expected value from the approved local override, then the deployment profile, then the vendor default, and keep that provenance in the finding.
checks.criterion: each enabled section meets expectations.thp, expectations.ksm, expectations.mitigations_off, expectations.vm_swappiness, expectations.cpu_governor, expectations.tuned_profile and expectations.net_mtu as the profile resolves them; a conflict between the local override and the vendor default is reported as unresolved, not decided.

checks.goal: Every xiRAID array is online with all members present and a valid licence.
checks.procedure: Cross-check the xiraid.* checks, the baseline storage section and arrays.list. Link each array to its member disks and to the filesystem it backs (health.context.topology).
checks.criterion: every array state is online, no member is missing or failed, the licence is valid and the xiRAID service is active.

checks.goal: A reconstruction or initialisation is progressing, not stalled.
checks.procedure: Read the array's progress, then read the raid progress feed for an earlier sample inside the window. Compare the two samples' progress and time.
checks.criterion: two progress samples inside the window show increasing progress; a single sample yields unknown, never stalled.

checks.goal: No drive is failing: SMART critical flags, temperature, wear and PCIe link are within expectations.
checks.procedure: The nvme_health section is enabled only in the deep baseline profile; with another profile report the drives as not covered rather than healthy. Map each drive to the arrays it belongs to.
checks.criterion: no critical SMART flag; temperature under expectations.nvme_temp_warn and expectations.nvme_temp_fail; wear under expectations.nvme_wear_warn and expectations.nvme_wear_fail; every PCIe link at its negotiated width and speed.

checks.goal: Per-disk health from the control path's own observations.
checks.procedure: No collector observes SMART today: the deterministic disk.health check reports that no collector exists. Use HC-04.drives (the baseline engine) instead and list this row under Not checked.
checks.criterion: not evaluable in this release.

checks.goal: Every managed filesystem is mounted where desired, with the desired options and headroom.
checks.procedure: Cross-check the mount check, the baseline filesystem section and filesystems.get for each target filesystem; read quotas.list where quota mode is on. Write availability is only ever proven by HC-12.
checks.criterion: mounted as desired; usage under expectations.fs_usage_warn and expectations.fs_usage_fail; inodes under expectations.fs_inode_warn and expectations.fs_inode_fail; mount options as desired.

checks.goal: The NFS server is active with the desired threads, versions and transport.
checks.procedure: Service active, export declared and client works are three separate questions: this row is the first. Compare the running server with the desired NFS profile.
checks.criterion: nfs-server is active; threads equal expectations.nfs_threads; the enabled versions and RDMA transport match the desired profile.

checks.goal: Every desired share is exported as declared and the server logs no RPC errors in the window.
checks.procedure: Compare desired shares with the effective export table, then read the current sessions and the logs bounded to the run window. An absent or truncated log is a data gap, not evidence of no errors.
checks.criterion: each desired share is exported with the declared clients and options; RPC or export errors inside the window are findings.

checks.goal: A real client can reach and mount the export.
checks.procedure: No producer: neither the node nor the api observes a client. In service_path scope this is HC-11.client-path; the loopback probe of HC-12 proves only the node's own path.
checks.criterion: not evaluable from the node.

checks.goal: Links are up at the expected speed and MTU, one netplan file owns them, and RDMA is live.
checks.procedure: Cross-check the network.* checks (rdma-live needs the standard profile), the baseline network and rdma sections and network.interfaces.list. Error and drop growth needs two samples inside the window.
checks.criterion: exactly one netplan owner; every managed link up at expectations.net_speed_min and expectations.net_mtu; RDMA devices present with active ports; no error or drop growth across two samples (one sample: unknown).

checks.goal: The end-to-end MTU and the switch path to the clients match the node's configuration.
checks.procedure: No producer on the node: a path MTU or fabric check needs a client-side probe or switch telemetry. List it under Not checked.
checks.criterion: not evaluable from the node.

checks.goal: Required units are active and the host tuning matches the desired state.
checks.procedure: Cross-check systemd.units and tuning.sysctl with the baseline services, cpu, kernel, vm and perf_tuning sections; read the logs bounded to the run window for kernel and service errors.
checks.criterion: every required unit active; tuning equals expectations.cpu_governor, expectations.thp, expectations.vm_swappiness and expectations.nvme_poll_queues; kernel or service errors inside the window are findings.

checks.goal: Record the node's current performance counters as an observation with its time.
checks.procedure: Read the exporter text and the metrics once and keep the sample with its timestamp. Saturation claims need the exporter's own thresholds, never an invented one.
checks.criterion: a single sample is reported as an observation, not as a trend; a threshold breach is a finding only when the source defines the threshold.

checks.goal: Detect growth or degradation over the run window.
checks.procedure: Take a second metrics sample inside the window, or use one the client supplied, and compare with the first.
checks.criterion: a trend needs two samples inside the window; one sample yields unknown.

checks.goal: Find configuration changes, tasks and events inside the window that could explain a finding.
checks.procedure: Read the audit trail, the configuration snapshots and their diff, the task list and the system event feed, each bounded to the window and its retention. Report the difference between the requested and the available window.
checks.criterion: a change inside the window that touches an affected resource is a hypothesis, never a confirmed cause without a discriminating fact.

checks.goal: The authorised client mounts, reads and writes the export over the expected transport.
checks.procedure: No producer in this release: service_path coverage is partial until a client-side probe exists. State it in the Not checked section and in coverage_status.
checks.criterion: not evaluable in this release.

checks.goal: One confirmed active probe proves a write path or a loopback NFS mount on this node.
checks.procedure: Only when health.context permitted.probe_run is not denied and the effective probe policy is bounded_active; the host confirms each probe separately. Prefer one fs_io on the affected filesystem or one nfs_loopback on the affected share; never both by default.
checks.criterion: a passing probe proves only the operation it performed (the proves text): not client connectivity, not RDMA transport, not durability beyond fsync. A cleanup failure is a warning with the artifact path.
